doc.title: Carmen Lundy interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 15, 2023

title: Hearing jazz harmony from Dave Roitstein and joining the youth jazz band
summary: Her gospel and record-hearing background, first paying job in high school, and friend Dave Roitstein introducing her to Bill Evans-style piano and the Youth Jazz Band.

bands.name: University of Miami Youth Jazz Band

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Yeah. Was there a particular reason that you switched from opera study to jazz?

Yes. Let’s see, I’m going to try and make a synopsis of the whole time. When I entered the University of Miami, having the background that we just talked about — I had a cousin who is an incredible blues guitarist and all this beautiful music happening in my life, I had an aunt who was best friends with the guy that owned the record store so she had everything, you know every new release from everybody and we’d have to go over to her house to hear that stuff because we couldn’t listen to it at our own house. So I had already this wonderful exposure to beautiful music prior to becoming serious at that point or from high school. But I was already — I had my first paying job in my junior year of high school with the [s/l] Alshuen Stage Band singing Dionne Warwick and Roberta Flack and blah-blah. When I got to the University of Miami two things happened. I had become friends with a young accompanist in high school, his name was Dave Roitstein who happens to be receiving a Lifetime Achievement at the University of Miami next week, but he’s the head of CalArts Music School Jazz Department here in Los Angeles. Now David was the accompanist for the choir in high school. And when I asked him to play for me, because I was always the one playing for, you know, some of my classmates for the talent shows, I asked him to play for me because I really wanted to step out and sing and not have to do this whole piano-sing thing. And when he accompanied me there was something so different about the sound of his piano than my piano. I had come from that Gospel thing, you know second inversions and all that stuff. And David was playing major seventh and ninths and I was like, “What are you doing?” So he was just kind of like just a generous person, you know his nature. He said, “Oh I’m studying Bill Evans right now and I’m playing jazz piano and I’m studying jazz piano. And I’m like, “What is that?” So our friendship just blossomed from that. And by the time I got to the University of Miami I was still in this classical track, I was on this classical track. And David and I had formed a couple of little performances during that summer period before the freshman year. So we were just doing pop tunes, you know like for nursing homes and things like that, and he would bring his Fender Rhodes and set it up and you know we would do our thing. So right in that patch he joined the University of Miami Youth Jazz Band and they needed a vocalist. And that’s what happened.
